note: min/max of params and timing are UI bounds chosen by the registry author unless a measured value is attached; null = unknown; engine.available = the new engine (bti.engine) can render this technique today (engine.impl is its renderer, engine.reason says why not); param.required = must be present (default null); param types point, box, camera, asset, text were added for the engine

techniques.name: Push-in
techniques.description: A slow 2D crop that enlarges on the artwork, drifting toward a detail.
techniques.usage_rule: Used while the narration dwells on a region, so the eye moves in as the point is made; crops lead from whole or group toward face, hands or texture (Sargent portrait push to the face, Goya Saturn push on black).

engine.notes: Params are the explicit camera keys (rel anchors by default); default_params builds them from style.json camera_presets (the old zoom_ratio/focus/easing knobs are now generator inputs, not stored params).

techniques.name: Layered relative motion
techniques.description: Foreground figures and the background plate move and scale at different rates, giving a sense of depth.
techniques.usage_rule: Great Wave 45-80 s keeps one composition while foreground wave, boat and Fuji shift relative to each other as narration moves from observation to interpretation.

engine.notes: Foreground (image + aligned mask) and background each follow their own camera track; fg_zoom/bg_zoom/easing build a centred push only when a track is not given. Zoom interpolates linearly by default (benchmark); set zoom_interp log for the engine's other cameras. Needs a clean background plate registered to the foreground for a good result.

techniques.name: Pull-back
techniques.description: The crop shrinks and widens until the whole painting and its matte edge are revealed.
techniques.usage_rule: Opens an episode (decelerating pull-back to the full painting on the matte) and closes it (very slow pull-out of about 40 s); also used to return to the whole work after a detail.

engine.notes: Params are the explicit camera keys (rel anchors by default); default_params builds them from style.json camera_presets (the old zoom_ratio/focus/easing knobs are now generator inputs, not stored params).

evidence: measurements.md opening 3.0x/17.9 s and closing 5.8x/40 s

techniques.name: Pan up
techniques.description: The frame glides upward over a tall image, revealing forehead and eyes while the chin leaves the bottom edge.
techniques.usage_rule: Slow reveal along a vertical figure or garment (dress pan down in the Arnolfini episode, portrait pan up).

engine.notes: Params are the explicit camera keys (rel anchors by default); default_params builds them from style.json camera_presets (the old zoom_ratio/focus/easing knobs are now generator inputs, not stored params).

techniques.name: Zoom and shift
techniques.description: The crop enlarges while its centre travels toward a region, so zoom and drift happen together.
techniques.usage_rule: Used to travel from a pair or group to a specific detail (mirror push, chandelier push, hands push).

engine.notes: Params are the explicit camera keys (rel anchors by default); default_params builds them from style.json camera_presets (the old zoom_ratio/focus/easing knobs are now generator inputs, not stored params).

evidence: measurements.md mirror push 3.57x/11 s ease in-out

techniques.name: Hold and label reveal
techniques.description: The painting rests centred on the matte and a white label appears over it.
techniques.usage_rule: Opening or return-to-whole shot: hold the full work on the matte, then pop the title label.

engine.notes: Matte shot (camera as CAM-01; default whole picture) with a label strip: pop in at label_delay_s, hold label_hold_s, fade. Text comes from params (no text slot). Registry defaults reproduce the benchmark strip (y 70 %); default_params uses the channel measurements from style.json (y 79.4-93.3 %).

techniques.name: Dissolve
techniques.description: Two images overlap and one fades into the other in the same frame area.
techniques.usage_rule: Used for footage-to-painting change inside a panel; no dissolves were found in the Arnolfini episode, whose cuts are hard.

engine.notes: Used through transition_in; length is transition_in.dur.

techniques.name: Image slide in/out
techniques.description: An image enters from the edge into a cell beside the current image, then leaves the same way.
techniques.usage_rule: Brings a comparison work in next to the anchor painting and removes it again (Great Wave comparison, Sargent/Scream, Guernica strip).

engine.notes: Generic edge slide of the incoming shot over the outgoing one (transition_in). The episode's two-panel slide-in is a LAY-01 parameter.

techniques.name: Panel opening
techniques.description: Two side panels narrow in perspective and open to uncover the central picture.
techniques.usage_rule: Triptych reveal (Bosch): the closed wings open on the narration about opening them, then the inner scene is shown.

engine.notes: Ported from build_reel.py (tr03); content from slots/params.

techniques.name: Full-to-crop hard cut
techniques.label_vi: Cắt từ toàn cảnh vào chi tiết
techniques.description: The whole painting is replaced instantly by a crop of a detail.
techniques.usage_rule: Default way to go from the whole work to a detail; the label appears just after the cut.

engine.notes: A hard cut; the detail camera belongs to the next shot.

techniques.name: Two panels
techniques.description: Two images or crops sit side by side on the matte with a gap, each with a caption.
techniques.usage_rule: Anchor painting stays in one cell while the other cell shows a comparison work, drawing or photo.

engine.notes: Right panel slides in from the right edge (the episode's LAY-01 + TR-02). Each side has its own camera in its own image's source pixels.

techniques.name: Spotlight
techniques.description: The painting darkens and a soft ellipse around the subject stays bright.
techniques.usage_rule: Isolates a figure, table or statue while the narration discusses it, then restores the whole (Goya white-shirted figure, Last Supper table, Raphael statues).

engine.notes: Param names follow the design example (floor, ramp_in, ramp_out). ramp_out starts at the overlay end and runs past it (the shot clips it).

techniques.name: Progressive figure reveal
techniques.description: Figures fade or slide in group by group over an empty room.
techniques.usage_rule: Room first, then central figure, then groups (Last Supper, School of Athens): builds the reading order from space to people.

params.name: slide_from
params.pattern_hint: Mỗi dòng một hướng: none, left, right, top hoặc bottom

engine.notes: Base shot: plate (dimmed) with groups revealed through masks mask_1..mask_6, each fading in while sliding from slide_from[k] (left, right, top, bottom, none; cycled). Plate, figures and masks share one coordinate system; one camera track (compose over the matte). The benchmark's plate is an inpainted stand-in; supply a clean plate for a real result.

techniques.name: Colour kept on subject
techniques.description: The subject keeps its colour while the rest turns monochrome.

engine.notes: Overlay: the frame goes monochrome outside the mask (slot mask, aligned to the shot image). restore_s 0 keeps it until the overlay ends.

techniques.name: Circle draw
techniques.description: One or two rings are drawn around a small detail, held, then fade.
techniques.usage_rule: Marks small objects named in the narration (candles, roundels, lines in a document); two rings appear one after the other.

engine.notes: Radius is in source pixels (scales with the camera); diameter_pct_width is only used by default_params. Nothing is drawn at or after the overlay end.

techniques.name: Object outline
techniques.description: A white line traces the edge of a figure group.
techniques.usage_rule: Goya 1058-1129: outlines on soldiers and the two sides make the anonymity and opposition claims visible; Last Supper outlines four groups one at a time and then removes them.

engine.notes: Progressive outline: contours of the mask slot (longest max_contours) or the polyline `points` (source px). Fades out ending at the overlay end; dims the base to dim_base while it is shown (0.85 in the benchmark).

techniques.name: Perspective rays
techniques.description: White lines converge on a vanishing point, appear one by one, then vanish.
techniques.usage_rule: Raphael 670-695 s: horizontal and converging lines build one-point perspective that leads to the two central figures.

engine.notes: Rays drawn one by one from origins (fractions of the frame, or source px when origin_space=source) to the vanishing point (source px); ray_count uses the first N origins. dim_base default here is 0.8.

techniques.name: Map circle and arrow
techniques.label_vi: Vòng và mũi tên trên bản đồ
techniques.description: A ring and an arrowed route appear on a satellite map, with a place label.
techniques.usage_rule: Starry Night 699-710 s: moves from painting/drawing comparison to a map explaining where the village lies.

engine.notes: Rings + labels on `places`, arrowed Bezier route from the first to the last (control point, or bend). background: auto = the `map` slot image if present (positions in map px), else the procedural stand-in map (canvas px); base = draw over the parent shot (source px). Defaults are canvas px of the procedural map.

techniques.name: Dimension ruler
techniques.description: White measuring lines with numbers (60 cm, 82 cm) and a medium caption pop onto a picture.
techniques.usage_rule: Appears when the narration states a size or the thickness of a layer; all pieces appear within 0.2 s and stay at least 3.2 s.

engine.notes: Rulers follow the image rectangle on screen; frame_zoom (optional) pins the rectangle centred at that zoom regardless of camera.

techniques.name: Grid and geometric regions
techniques.description: A thirds grid and translucent triangles laid over the painting.

engine.notes: Grid (cols x rows) and one translucent region. shape_points: triangle uses 3 points, rect 2 opposite corners, circle centre + a point on its edge; space frame = fractions of the canvas, image = source px. Fixes the benchmark, whose region blend also darkened the whole frame by region_opacity.

techniques.name: Dot field densifying
techniques.description: Faint coloured dots multiply into a dense dot field.

engine.notes: Base shot on the matte (camera as any matte shot): seeded dot positions, colours sampled from the live picture, count and radius follow the curves over densify_frac of the shot, then cross-fade to the picture.

techniques.name: Chapter title on blurred image
techniques.label_vi: Tiêu đề chương trên ảnh mờ
techniques.description: White small-caps chapter title centred over a blurred, darkened picture.
techniques.usage_rule: Opens a new section; the picture behind is the work's own image blurred (Techniques card over two blurred images).

engine.notes: ported from build_reel txt01; variant white_card = brown text on a white card (no image needed)

techniques.name: Sliding italic text
techniques.description: Large white italic lines move horizontally across a background image.
techniques.usage_rule: Review text priority over context image (Sargent critics 1096.8-1102 s).

engine.notes: ported from build_reel txt02; overlay: the picture is the shot's own image, dimmed by background_dim (brightness multiplier)

techniques.name: Black matte
techniques.description: A vertical painting is shown at full height, centred on a black matte; detail crops are full-bleed 16:9.
techniques.usage_rule: Whole works sit on the matte; details fill the frame with no matte.

engine.notes: Params are the explicit camera keys (rel anchors by default); default_params builds them from style.json camera_presets (the old zoom_ratio/focus/easing knobs are now generator inputs, not stored params). Backdrop is the benchmark's near-black radial gradient with soft shadow (shadow=true), not the channel's pure black.

techniques.description: A grey map with a red route or dotted line.

engine.notes: Plain text glued to a point (`at`, source px) or fixed on screen (`screen`, canvas px). Leader lines are not implemented.

techniques.name: Year centred on image
techniques.description: A large white year centred over a blurred or dark image.
techniques.usage_rule: Date captions on the matte (1433 / 1434 in the Arnolfini build).

engine.notes: Overlay over the shot's image (not a standalone background card).

techniques.name: Grid and projection rays
techniques.description: A grid next to a skewed smear, with rays built up from a point at left.

engine.notes: Mechanism ported: grid + lettered columns over a crop of any image, ray fan grown from one point. Still needs real material from a human to look like the channel: an anamorphic image (skull smear) in slot `image`; rays are straight lines to a fan, not computed from the anamorphosis.

techniques.name: Two views of one object
techniques.description: Two states or viewing angles show a distorted shape resolving into a skull.

engine.notes: Mechanism ported: one image flat and warped by a perspective quad (from_quad -> to_quad). Needs a human to supply the anamorphic image and tune to_quad to the real oblique angle; the benchmark used a mirror crop.

techniques.name: Cross-section and light rays
techniques.description: A layered cross-section with names; gold rays go down and bounce up in a V.
techniques.usage_rule: Mona Lisa 483-533 s: reference section shown, layer names pointed out, gold V rays drawn, layers appear, then a measuring arrow with the thickness (about 40 micrometres).

params.name: layers
params.pattern_hint: Mỗi dòng: TÊN | #màu | độ dày, ví dụ OAK PANEL | #785a3c | 200

engine.notes: Schematic bands from the `layers` param ('NAME | #rrggbb | height'); with a real cross-section/micrograph in slot `cross_section` the image is drawn and the names are overlaid. Needs a real cross-section image from a human to look like the channel. Optional measuring arrow via measure_text.

techniques.name: Figure and separated pieces

engine.notes: Fill -> outline -> image stages from `stages` lines; a `footage` video stage is supported. Needs a human-made silhouette `mask` and, for the channel look, real process footage; without footage the final stage is the reference image.

techniques.name: Room model and UV image

engine.notes: Room image slot (else a wireframe schematic), painting_box marker, and a detail image crossfading to a real UV photograph. Needs a real room render/photo and a real UV capture from a human; the benchmark simulated UV with a false-colour map (not part of the renderer).

techniques.usage_rule: Seen in an announcement/promo short, not the main films.

engine.notes: Overlay: coloured box + label near the bottom of a 9:16 panel (put it on a SHORT-* shot). The benchmark's clipped label is fixed (text centred in the box). Content-complete; box_color defaults to the channel-measured yellow.

techniques.name: Colour wheel from palette
techniques.description: A circle split into colour sectors in an archive image.
techniques.usage_rule: Only a still was seen; no animation is established.

engine.notes: Colour wheel from k-means colours of slot `palette` (seeded, cached). Only a still of this was seen on the channel, so the sector build-up animation is our own. A human should supply a palette/archive image that matches the topic.

techniques.name: Hard cut
techniques.description: The picture changes instantly between two shots with no fade, dissolve or wipe.
techniques.usage_rule: Default between every pair of base shots; all sampled cuts in the Arnolfini episode are hard (no dissolve at card-to-image or black-to-card).

engine.notes: The channel default; normally written as transition_in: null.

techniques.usage_rule: Marks a chapter boundary; text pops in over 0.1 s shortly after the card starts and leaves before the hard cut.

techniques.usage_rule: Appears just after a cut to a detail crop, names the object, stays about 3.2 s, then disappears.

techniques.name: Recap labels at closing
techniques.description: Plain white words (for example CANDLE, ROUNDELS, MOURNING DRESS, DOG) placed near their details over the black matte, with no strip.
techniques.usage_rule: In the closing pull-out the details are named again, one at a time, as the narration recalls them.

engine.notes: Same renderer as STATIC-08 with a larger default size.

techniques.name: Sequential group outlines
techniques.description: White outlines are drawn around groups one after another, then all disappear while the whole painting stays.
techniques.usage_rule: Last Supper 21:11-21:25: the four groups of three are outlined in turn; Goya: outline soldiers, then both sides.

engine.notes: Outlines drawn group by group from slots mask_1..mask_6 (or params points_1..points_6). after_hold keep: outlines stay and (clear_all_at_end) all fade together ending at the overlay end; clear: each fades fade_s after hold_s. per_group_draw_s null spreads the groups over the overlay duration.

techniques.name: Map point markers one by one
techniques.label_vi: Chấm đánh dấu bản đồ lần lượt
techniques.description: Red dots appear one by one on a map.

engine.notes: Markers pop in one by one (stagger_s) with an optional pulse ring and label. Same background options as AN-04; marker_count null uses all points.

techniques.name: Stills sequence with fixed holds
techniques.label_vi: Chuỗi ảnh tĩnh giữ cố định
techniques.description: Several context stills follow each other, each held a fixed 4.0 s with a hard cut between them.
techniques.usage_rule: Stock or reference stills in a sequence are held exactly 4.0 s each (cuts at 181.3, 185.3, 189.3, 193.3 s).

engine.notes: One context still per shot (a return to the painting is a second shot). Label strip is a separate X-ANN-02 overlay. Default camera: image at 94 % height, 1.06x push over the shot.

evidence: ref/qa_pacing2.txt (build holds median 7.4 s vs 4.0 s reference)

techniques.name: Swap one side of a split
techniques.label_vi: Đổi một bên của màn hình chia
techniques.description: The anchor painting stays in one cell while the other cell's image or video is replaced by another comparison.
techniques.usage_rule: Starry Night 643-741 s: the painting stays left while the photo, Japanese print, map, village photo and church change on the right; Supper hand drawings swap while the left one stays.

engine.notes: New (no reel segment); built from the research description.

techniques.name: Wipe compare
techniques.description: A monochrome version enters from the right edge, a vertical border sweeps left, the two versions sit side by side, then dissolve to the colour image.
techniques.usage_rule: Mona Lisa about 554 s (dense-0554): shows two states of the same picture and returns to colour.

engine.notes: New (no reel segment); built from the research description. CMP-05 is the reel version (a single wipe of two colour states).

techniques.name: Strip slides in, then splits
techniques.label_vi: Dải trượt vào rồi chia đôi
techniques.description: A strip from a second work slides up from the bottom into a full-frame image, then moves right so it sits beside the first painting.
techniques.usage_rule: Goya 1119-1129: a Guernica strip slides up, fills the frame, then separates to the right to compare with Goya.

techniques.name: Dim to isolate then restore

techniques.description: The whole frame darkens around a figure or object that stays bright, then brightness returns and the frame widens back.
techniques.usage_rule: Goya 1088-1109 and 1139-1155, Raphael statues 721-747, Supper table 21:25: dim, dwell, restore to the whole.

techniques.usage_rule: Overlay on the first shot of a video, from its start (nominal 9.0 s). The camera of the shot is not changed. Style `raking` of the channel identity.

engine.notes: Light only (a gain on the frame, soft band at reduced resolution). Nominal length = sweep_start_s + sweep_s + release_s. Times are nominal seconds from the start of the element; a shorter element scales them (actual / nominal length), a longer one keeps them.

techniques.name: Time axis with dates
techniques.description: A time axis with dates on the dark ground of the channel: a hairline axis grows from the left, ticks fade in, and each dated item grows a stalk from the axis and fades in its year and a short label at its own time. The technique chooses, for every item, the side of the axis, the length of the stalk and the place of the label so that no label touches another label or another stalk and every label stays inside the frame (two items or twelve, two in the same year, BC and AD together). At `focus_s` the accented item brightens, gets a dot on the axis, and the others dim.
techniques.usage_rule: Use it when the narration places events in time: a run of dated events ("in 1425 ... in 1431 ... in 1434"), a span, the order of things. It is a dark shot of its own (no picture). Give `items`, one per dated moment the narration names: `date` (a whole year, negative for BC), `label` (a few words of your own, at most 48 characters, never a sentence of the narration), `at` (seconds from the start of the shot, or the word that names the event so that its stalk grows on that word), `side` (leave `auto`: the technique picks the side, the stalk length and the label's place) and `accent` true on the one moment the sentence is about (it brightens at `focus_s`, the others dim). Leave `from`, `to` empty and `tick_every` 0 unless the axis must run wider than the items (empty `from`/`to` = the items' range with one year of margin; a date outside the axis is an error). One to 12 items; items too close together to be laid out are refused. The default data is an example (Van Eyck, 1425 to 1434): ALWAYS replace all of `items`. Dates come from the narration and the project's sources: leave an item out rather than guess a year. Let the shot last about one second per item plus three.

engine.notes: Dark ground #131519, text #E9E2D0, hairlines #8D877A. Times are seconds from the start of the shot (or word anchors in an item's `at`). The axis grows over 0.8 s; a stalk grows over 0.35 s from its `at`, the year fades in from +0.2 s, the label from +0.35 s; from `focus_s` (0.8 s ramp) the others dim to `dim_to`. Layout: depth first search over side, stalk length (3 above the axis, 2 below) and label place, accented items first; unsolvable data is refused (`time_crowded`). Label cap height `cap_pct`, the year is 1.44 times larger (EB Garamond, bundled).

techniques.name: Relations: family and patrons
techniques.label_vi: Sơ đồ quan hệ: gia đình và người bảo trợ
techniques.description: Relations between people on the dark ground of the channel: names with a smaller second line (dates or role), hairline connectors drawn one after another, a marriage as a short horizontal line between two names of one row, descent running down in right angles, relations such as patron or painter drawn the same way, and small italic edge labels. When `row` and `col` are left out the technique lays the tree out itself: generations by descent, spouses side by side, crossings reduced, everything inside the frame (the text is made smaller when the tree is wide).
techniques.usage_rule: Use it when the narration explains who is related to whom or who worked for whom: a family, a patron and the painters he hired, a workshop, who married whom, who painted or bought which work. It is a dark shot of its own (no picture). `nodes`: `id` (short, no spaces), `name`, `sub` (a smaller second line: dates or a role), `strong` true for the one or two names the sentence is about, `at` (seconds from the start of the shot, or the word that names the person so that the name appears on it). `edges`: `from`, `to` (ids), `kind` (`descent` from parent to child, `marriage` between two names, `link` for any other relation such as patron to painter or painter to work), `label` (two or three words in small italic, for example 'married 1426'), `at` (when the line is drawn, from `from` to `to`). Leave `row` and `col` at -1: the technique lays the tree out itself (parents above children, spouses side by side); give both for every name only to place them by hand. Two to 14 names, at most five generations, a person has at most two marriages; a tree that cannot fit is refused. The default data is an example (Philip the Good, Van Eyck, the Arnolfini): ALWAYS replace `nodes` and `edges` together. Names, dates and relations come from the narration and the project's sources: leave out anything you are unsure of rather than guess. Let the shot last about one second per name plus three.

techniques.name: The same picture in two states
techniques.label_vi: Cùng một tranh ở hai trạng thái
techniques.description: The same picture in two states (colour and infrared, before and after a restoration): two image slots of the same crop framed by one camera that does not move during a change, a dissolve from one to the other and back, holds given as text, and the name of the state in small capitals at the bottom left with a soft shadow.
techniques.usage_rule: Use it when the narration shows one picture in two states: before and after a restoration, colour and infrared, the underdrawing, a reconstruction of the original colours. It needs two images of the SAME crop (slot `a` and slot `b`; the owner chose them): if the project has no second image of the picture, do not use it. `label_a` and `label_b` name the two states in a word or two ("Colour", "Infrared", "Before", "After"); `first` says which is seen first; `holds` is how long each state is held, in seconds, written "1.5; 2.5; 1.5" (the first state, then the other, then the first again; two to six numbers); `dissolve_s` is the length of each change. The shot's `camera` frames both pictures and does not move during a change. Let the shot last the holds plus one dissolve between each pair (7.5 s for the default). The change is the point: start the shot so that the dissolve falls on the word that names the new state.

params.pattern_hint: Gõ một dòng, tối đa 32 ký tự: tên của trạng thái ở hình a, ví dụ Colour; để trống thì không có chữ.

params.name: holds

engine.notes: Both pictures are drawn as CAM-01 draws one (the camera of the shot, in source pixels of slot `a`; image b is scaled to the width of a and centred on it, so images of one crop line up at any resolution). Timeline in seconds from the start of the shot: hold, linear dissolve, hold ... as `holds` and `dissolve_s` say; the last state is held to the end of the shot. The camera clock stops during a dissolve. A hold is exactly the picture of its state. Caption: small capitals (EB Garamond Regular, tracking 0.14 em, cap height `label_cap_pct`) at 4.5 percent from the left, fades in at 0.3 s, flips through a fade at the middle of each dissolve, fades out ending 0.1 s before the end.

techniques.name: Atlas map
techniques.description: A map of real geography (Natural Earth, bundled, no network) drawn like an atlas plate: paper land, a blue-grey or sepia sea that is darker toward the coast with two water lines, an ink coastline, small place marks with italic labels that appear on the word that names them, a dotted route drawn with a travelling head, an optional tinted country, sea names, and a slow push from a wide view to a view fitted to the places.
techniques.usage_rule: Use it for ANY place, journey or territory a sentence names (where a painter lived or travelled, where a work was made, shipped or kept, a country's extent). It replaces STATIC-06, AN-04 and X-ANN-05 for new work (they stay valid for old storyboards). Give: `places` (id, name, lonlat [longitude, latitude], `at` = seconds from the start of the shot or a word anchor so the mark lands on the word that names the place), `route` (from/to place ids, `via` points that bend it; pass [] for no route), `region_iso` (ISO codes of today's countries to tint; [] for none) and `region_label`. The default data is an example (Bruges to Lucca with Belgium): ALWAYS set places, route and region_iso together, or the example's route and region remain. Coordinates are yours to supply; leave a place out rather than guess it. The view runs from `view_start_width_km` to the end view (`fit` of all places with `view_end_margin_pct`, or `manual` with a centre and width). Let the shot last 6 to 10 s.
